chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Aamir ibn al-Simt, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) – similar to it.

Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ali ibn Ja'far ibn Ishaq al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The wine is from five: the juice from the grapes, the marinade from the raisins, the mead from the honey, the ale from the barley, and Al-Nabeez from the dates.
ai.seo_question: What are the five sources of wine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through prominent chains in al-Kafi, explicitly categorizes the five primary ingredients—grapes, raisins, honey, barley, and dates—that yield wine (khamr) according to Shia jurisprudence. It provides the essential botanical basis for distinguishing between specific types of intoxicants and their legal status, reinforcing the Prophet's definition which underpins the broader prohibition of intoxicants in Islamic law.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Safwan Al Jammal, from Aamir Bin Al Samt, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> – similar to it.

Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabir, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajaj, from Ali Bin Ja’far Bin Is’haq Al Hashimy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘
The wine is from five – the juice from the grapes, and the marinade from the raisins, and the mead from the honey, and the ale from the barley, and Al-Nabeez from the dates’.
en.sarwar: Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajj aj from Ali ibn Ja‘far ibn Ishaq al-Hashimiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Wine is made of five substances: it is made from grape juice, extracts of raisins, al-Bit ’ (mead) from honey, al-Mizru (beer) from barley and wine from dates.’”
